messages:
Sanjay: FYI support ticket from Acme: customers in APAC reporting huge p99 spikes for text-generation calls to hosted API since ~04:00 UTC. First report shows TLS handshake timeouts and some 504s. Escalating.
Liz M: @Sanjay thanks — do we have region/route info from the customer? orig IPs? any traceroutes? brief repro steps would help.
Sanjay: Provided IPs and sample curl. They call https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with a 512-token prompt. Sample curl timings show CONNECT and SSL phases taking 400-700ms each occasionally. Here's the customer's curl --trace-time output (sanitized):

Evan: paste below — looks like a cross-AZ hop causing extra RTTS. trace from one of our egress IPs to client ASN shows a sudden detour through SG -> JP -> AU.

Evan: ```
traceroute to 203.0.113.47 (203.0.113.47), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.40.1.1 (10.40.1.1)  0.20 ms  0.19 ms  0.18 ms
 2  203.0.113.1 (203.0.113.1)  12.1 ms  12.0 ms  12.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.5 (198.51.100.5)  120.9 ms  121.3 ms  121.0 ms
 4  198.51.100.13 (198.51.100.13)  230.4 ms  231.0 ms  229.8 ms
 5  203.0.113.47 (203.0.113.47)  232.1 ms  231.7 ms  231.9 ms
```

Evan: That's the interesting part — hop 2 is our edge POP in SG, hop 3 jumps to a different provider path (maybe JP backbone) before getting back. I see increased TLS handshake retries in our edge logs for that POP starting 03:58 UTC.
Julia: Any recent changes to our global route/anycast config? I know we had a candidate BGP prep change pushed yesterday to try prefer nearby colo for low-cost paths.
Alex: I rolled that BGP prep candidate through two hours ago for APAC (small prefix prep). Could be related. I can roll it back if ops agrees.
Liz M: Before rollback can we confirm: 1) DNS lookup results in the client region? 2) Are we seeing certificate renegotiation / new TLS handshakes (no session reuse) in the edge logs? 3) Did the CDN/edge change alter TLS ciphers or ALPN?
Evan: Answers:
- DNS: dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short from Tokyo shows 203.0.113.1 (our SG edge). But some clients in AU resolve a different anycast-advertised IP that now routes through JP backbone.
- TLS: logs show spike in TLS full-handshakes (no session_resumed) and occasional fatal handshake_failure in the TLS record layer.
- Ciphers: no config change on ciphers. ALPN unchanged.

Evan: Extract from edge log (simplified):
```
[03:59:12 UTC] pop=sg1 client=203.0.113.47 tls_handshake=full time_ms=542 retry=1
[03:59:14 UTC] pop=sg1 client=203.0.113.47 tls_handshake=full time_ms=614 retry=2
[04:01:05 UTC] pop=ap-syd client=203.0.113.47 tls_handshake=full time_ms=950 retry=1
```

Sanjay: Customer says this started after a maintenance window on their ISP, but we saw the same spike across multiple customers in APAC so likely our routing change made a bad path more common.
Julia: Hypothesis: BGP prep caused certain regions to prefer a path that crosses an extra backbone hop, increasing RTT and causing more TLS timeouts (clients with low TCP/TLS timeouts see 504s). Also TLS session reuse broken because session tickets might be pinned to a specific POP — if routing makes a different POP answer subsequent requests, session reuse fails.
Alex: quick mitigation options:
- rollback BGP prep (fast) — likely immediate improvement but needs coordination with infra on what prefixes to revert.
- enable session-ticket replication across POPs for a short window (medium difficulty) so TLS resumption works even on different POPs.
- add policy to prefer local-region POPs via our smart-router (hotfix rule) — low risk.
Liz M: Rollback + smart-router pin sounds good. Can we do rollback now and monitor p99 for APAC for 30m? If rollback helps we can then revert the BGP change in the staging config permanently.
Alex: I'll initiate rollback now. deploy-bot will show steps.

deploy-bot: Initiating route-prep rollback for prefixes affecting apac. Started at 04:12:01 UTC. Change ID: RB-2026-411

Evan: Kicking off metric checks — p99 latency graph for ap-southeast1 before rollback: 980ms at peak, after starting rollback I already see drop to ~220ms in a subset of traces.
Sanjay: Customer confirms improved experience, retries are down, and no more 504s for last 10 minutes.
Liz M: Great. Next actions:
- Alex: open PR to permanently remove the problematic BGP prep or narrow scope + add canarying rules
- Evan: run a sweep to ensure session tickets are replicated or consider moving to TLS 1.3 0-RTT safe modes for session resumption where possible
- Julia: update runbook and incident note (include traceroutes, dig outputs and the BGP change ID)

Alex: Will do PR and add a canary window for next deploy. ETA PR by EOD.
Evan: I'll run an automated traceroute/bgp path monitor over APAC POPs to detect regressions and alert at 5% increased median hop count.
Julia: Filing the followup incident ticket now. Good catch everyone.

Sanjay: Thanks team. Closing thread once followups are in the ticket. :thumbsup:
